RaceName: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Wins in Bahrain (6f, good to firm) and at Ascot (5f, good to firm) this summer; stiff task under a penalty in the Stewards' Cup 18 days ago and ran respectably in midfield; the Ascot form makes him of interest and he could prove suited by this intermediate trip; whether his high draw proves beneficial remains to be seen though.

RaceName: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Looked one to follow when bolting up at Wolverhampton (6f, AW) in December and, after a series of misfortunes befell him early in the year, things have finally clicked this summer; saw off his 20 rivals over 6f here last month and then went down all guns blazing in the Stewards' Cup; another 3lb higher today but may not have reached his ceiling; high draw could be a negative.

RaceName: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Has plenty of ability (two Group-race wins in Dubai) but slow starts have crept in, notably in the Stewards' Cup 18 days ago; the experiment with blinkers has been quickly aborted but he is a risky proposition for now.

RaceName: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Coaxed back to his best by the Quinns this year, winning 6f handicaps here and at Chester and then running a fine race in a hot sprint handicap at the Curragh last month; weakened in the closing stages of the Stewards' Cup, a race in which he was 5lb well in, and a personal best is needed to defy this highest mark of his career over the shortest trip he will have tackled.

RaceName: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Successful in 5f handicaps twice last September having moved to Ed Bethell; beaten favourite on his first three starts this year, including here, but still ran to a useful level; managed to put his head in front, just, at Hamilton (5f, good) 18 days ago and although a 3lb rise didn't look overly generous, the third has won since; still has potential after just nine runs.

RaceName: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Better than ever this year following a gelding operation, winning at Goodwood (5f, good) in May and running with credit at Epsom (the Dash) and Glorious Goodwood since; should give his running but might find one or two better treated today.

RaceName: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Won last season's Ayr Silver Cup off a 5lb lower mark; has not had much luck this year, banging his head in the stalls in the Wokingham and then suffering a slipped saddle at Goodwood three weeks ago; for one so well suited by 6f and slow ground, today's test may be insufficient.

RaceName: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Had some strong form as a 3yo, including at York, and he returned to action in March with a good third at Southwell (5f, AW); two heavy defeats have followed (had a wind op after the first) and he arrives with a point to prove.

RaceName: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
OwnerName: L Bond & Sheikh Aymen Jawad Al Hamandi
Spotlight: He has performed with credit in all three York runs; two fine runs at Glorious Goodwood, notably in the Stewards' Cup in which he would have gone very close to winning granted a clear run at a crucial stage; races off the same mark and has a big run in him.

RaceName: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
OwnerName: Julie Martin & David R Martin & Partner
Spotlight: Travelled powerfully before wearing down The Man close home in this race 12 months ago; he arrives 3lb higher this time around, penalised for last week's Windsor success (a race in which he was second before his win here last year); whether his draw in stall 20 is a positive remains to be seen though.

RaceName: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Irish raider; he has run some solid races in defeat this summer but this looks a tough race in which to try to end a four-year drought.

RaceName: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: On the up for new trainer this year, winning 5f handicaps at Yarmouth and Southwell before a fine second at Glorious Goodwood (5f, good) three weeks ago, hitting the front 110 yards from home but picked off late on by a thriving opponent; 3lb rise asks a stiffer question.

RaceName: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
OwnerName: Hambleton Racing Ltd XXXI And Partner
Spotlight: Had a fine year in 2025, winning four times including in Listed and Group 3; not in comparable form  in 2026 but he has too much ability to be discounted completely.

RaceName: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Three front-running AW wins in the spring saw him soar up the handicap; ran right up to his best when second of ten in a Shergar Cup race at Ascot (5f, good to firm) 11 days ago; runs off the same mark but this looks a deeper event.

RaceName: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Took advantage of his drop in the weights at Goodwood (6f, soft) in June; down the field in the Wokingham at Royal Ascot; can win more races off this mark but perhaps not this one.

RaceName: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Fine servant to connections down the years; retains ability but he wasn't at his best here last month and younger rivals may have his measure.

RaceName: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Coaxed back to form by James Owen last autumn; had an unsuccessful stint in the Middle East over the winter but returned to Owen and won handicaps at Leicester (6f) and Salisbury (5f) in the spring; sold for 25,000gns last month; looks on a tough mark ahead of his stable debut.

RaceName: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Finished third behind Trefor and The Man in this race 12 months ago, having to wait for a gap but finishing off fastest of all; continued the good work this term, most recently finishing third of 21 to Stratusnine here (6f, good to firm) last month; 8lb better off with that rival for under one length; big run on the cards.

RaceName: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: 0-4 this year but retains ability; there's a slight concern that she will get taken off her feet early under these conditions and others appeal more.

RaceName: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Won a 5f handicap at last season's Dante meeting here and confirmed the track suited him well when collared late by Trefor in this race 12 months ago; 3lb lower this time around and he has done enough in 2026 to think he retains all his ability; trainer is making a name for himself in the big sprint handicaps and it's likely this has been the main aim all summer; big chance if getting it right at the start.

RaceName: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Course winner last month but has done all his winning at Class 4 level or lower; likely vulnerable in a race of this nature.

RaceName: Hong Kong Jockey Club World Pool Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Won a local Group 1 in Bahrain in January but got clobbered by the handicapper as a result; slipping back to a more realistic mark but drawn highest and others bring much more pressing claims.

RaceName: NXT Big Thing Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
OwnerName: Ursa Major Racing Ltd & Julie Camacho
Spotlight: 17,000gns yearling; sixth foal; Harry Angel half-sister to French 6.5f-1m2f winner El Torero; dam once-raced half-sister to winners Talbeyah (useful 8.5f-1m2f) and Sarrocchi (1m Listed), out of French 1m Listed winner; yard 0-5 with 2yos this season.

RaceName: NXT Big Thing Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Fading into fourth of six in a novice at Thirsk (7f, good to firm) last month was disappointing considering she was sent off at 8-13 for that debut, but she tried to match the well-bred winner 2f out; well-bred filly who can't be dismissed yet.

RaceName: NXT Big Thing Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Has a Group 1 Cheveley Park entry, which looks a long way removed from the form of her four 7f races; however, latest start was her best form (sixth of eight in a Listed race) and it gave plenty of hope, despite pedigree, that 6f will suit her better; should be a big player at this level.

RaceName: NXT Big Thing Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 17,000gns yearling by Ardad; sixth foal; half-sister to French 6.5f-1m2f winner El Torero; dam once-raced half-sister to winners Talbeyah (useful 8.5f-1m2f) and Sarrocchi (1m Listed), out of French 1m Listed winner; trainer's 2yos have made their mark this season, so she needs a market check.

RaceName: NXT Big Thing Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 4l fifth of eight at 100-1 in a maiden at Ayr (6f, good to soft) nine days ago was a lot better than her debut and the hood used that day is retained; this race should also demand better.

RaceName: NXT Big Thing Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Debut form at Ayr (7f, good; 40-1) seems better than her fourth of ten at Catterick (7f, good to firm; 8-1) 16 days later, but she does possess some ability.

RaceName: NXT Big Thing Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: By Naval Crown; first foal; dam unraced half-sister to winners Laraaib (1m4f Group 3) and Arwaah (useful 1m2f) out of 1m 2yo/1m4f Listed winner; while the dam's side suggests longer trips, this newcomer needs a close look.

RaceName: Tattersalls Acomb Stakes (Group 3) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Led when fifth of seven in Group 2 Superlative Stakes at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) last month and showed improved form under more patient tactics for Listed win at Ascot (7f, good to firm) 13 days later; his dam was a Group 1 winner and he could continue to progress; respected.

RaceName: Tattersalls Acomb Stakes (Group 3) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Came clear with next-time-out winner when scoring on nursery debut here (6f, good to firm) last month; the return to York could be a positive but he finished seventh of ten in the Group 2 Richmond at Glorious Goodwood (6f, good to firm) and others have a lot more substance to their claims.

RaceName: Tattersalls Acomb Stakes (Group 3) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Built upon the promise of his first two starts (debut here) to make all by 5l at Pontefract (6f, good) in June; respectable run in big field on nursery debut at Glorious Goodwood (6f, good to firm) last time but a chunk of improvement is necessary if he's to pose a serious threat today.

RaceName: Tattersalls Acomb Stakes (Group 3) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Won at Naas (6f, good) in May on second start before close sixth in the Coventry at Royal Ascot (6f, good to firm); third in 6.2f/6f Group races at the Curragh on next two runs; Ryan Moore rides stablemate Haffner but this 1,700,000gns yearling may take a step forward for 7f and is not ruled out.

RaceName: Tattersalls Acomb Stakes (Group 3) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Well backed when fifth on debut at Thirsk (7f, good) in May and displayed improvement for head win at Newbury (7f, good to firm) last month; Chaldean and Gewan won that same novice before following up in this race; unexposed and represents in-form yard but others have achieved more.

RaceName: Tattersalls Acomb Stakes (Group 3) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 105,000euros yearling who was backed into 4-1 when winning on debut at Salisbury (6f, good to firm) last month, when coming clear with a previous winner; he takes a leap in grade on this second start but looks a good prospect for 7f and his trainer won this in 2022 and 2025; interesting.

RaceName: Tattersalls Acomb Stakes (Group 3) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Won at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) last month on second start, before close second in the Group 2 Vintage Stakes at Glorious Goodwood (7f, good); he's in excellent hands to continue to progress and holds leading claims.

RaceName: Tattersalls Acomb Stakes (Group 3) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 4l win when odds-on for his debut at Yarmouth (6f, good to firm) in April and bounced back from heavy defeat at Royal Ascot to go close under a penalty in a novice at Newcastle (6f, AW) last month, when clear with an odds-on newcomer; however, it is likely that his limitations will be exposed today.

RaceName: Tattersalls Acomb Stakes (Group 3) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Runner-up over 6f here on first two starts (good) before keeping on strongly to win at Chester (6f, good) in June; improvement is necessary up in grade but his trainer has some useful 2yos and this colt shaped as though the step up to 7f could be a positive; not discounted.

RaceName: Tattersalls Acomb Stakes (Group 3) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Eye-catching third on debut at Fairyhouse (6f, good) in June and bounced back from disappointing run at the Curragh to make all in fine style at Galway (7f, yielding) last month; he's highly regarded by his Irish trainer and could have a big part to play.

RaceName: Tattersalls Acomb Stakes (Group 3) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Close fourth of five on debut at Ayr (7f, good to firm) last month and built on that to make all narrowly at Beverley (7.4f, good to firm) three weeks ago; that latest form has been franked and he represents a powerful 2yo stable, but he needs another step forward if he's to follow up this afternoon.

RaceName: Kingmoor Park Properties Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Won one of three bumpers; fourth this summer in her two races under Flat rules but there the similarity between them ends, as the first race was a AW maiden (9.4f) and the second a six-runner Group 3 at York (1m6f; 125-1); the latter was a slowly run affair but she came from last and was one of the fastest finishers, so a high rating should not be laughed out of court.

RaceName: Kingmoor Park Properties Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Half-sister to several winners, including two high-class ones, for her stable; third in small-field maidens at Lingfield (1m2f, good) and Doncaster (1m4f, good to firm) so she has ability, but Peace Belle has shown significantly more.

RaceName: Kingmoor Park Properties Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 4,000gns yearling; tenth foal; Advertise close relation to 5f 2yo/6f AW winner Red Showgirl (RPR 81), half-sister to four winners including Fantail (6f/1m, including 2yo; 88) and Fabulous Red (7f 2yo; 83); dam Listed-placed 9.7f winner (100); probably up against it on debut.

RaceName: Sky Bet Great Voltigeur Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
Spotlight: Galloped on relentlessly to win the Derby from Maltese Cross at Epsom, where nearly all the others sank without trace in the gruelling conditions, and ran just as well when he was again ridden prominently to finish second in the Irish Derby at the Curragh (1m4f, good; unraced on firmer) three weeks later, a neck in front of Pierre Bonnard; both of those rivals reoppose and he's now 5lb worse off with Pierre Bonnard, but won't go down without a fight.

RaceName: Sky Bet Great Voltigeur Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
Spotlight: His only defeat this season came at the hands of Christmas Day when second, beaten two and three-quarter lengths, in the Derby at Epsom (1m4f, soft); snatched the Group 1 Grand Prix de Paris at Longchamp (1m4f, good to firm) from the fire after trouble in running five weeks ago; has 5lb penalty but every race has brought improvement.

RaceName: Sky Bet Great Voltigeur Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
Spotlight: Twice made the running, including for 1m2f maiden win at Fairyhouse in June; disappointing on handicap debut next time and, as an inferior stablemate to two of the star acts in this field, probably set for front-running duties.

RaceName: Sky Bet Great Voltigeur Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
Spotlight: Steady improver in four-race career and he keeps on well for pressure, but this summer's 3l sixth of 11 at Royal Ascot (1m6f Group 2) and half-length second of five at Newmarket (1m5f Group 3, again good to firm) do not suggest he's a match for today's principals at 1m4f.

RaceName: Sky Bet Great Voltigeur Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
Spotlight: Looked every inch a serious Derby prospect last term, which he failed to confirm behind two of these in the mud at Epsom this June but the Irish Derby at the Curragh (1m4f, good) three weeks later addressed the doubts when he rallied well to finish just a neck behind runner-up Christmas Day; as he receives 5lb today from that rival and from Maltese Cross, that career-best performance puts him clear top on form.

RaceName: Sky Bet Great Voltigeur Stakes (Group 2) (Colts & Geldings)
Spotlight: 1,100,000gns yearling; won over 1m2f in a maiden at Leicester and novice at Newmarket, making all in the latter; passed a much tougher test with flying colours when 11-10 favourite for Listed race at Hamilton (1m3f, good to firm) in July, coming from fifth of six to assert gradually in the final 2f; keeps looking capable of better but today's company demands great deal more again.

RaceName: North Lakes Energy - Harry Doyle Memorial Maiden Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: Out of an Italian Oaks winner but she's yet to be placed and has been well held in four runs for new yard this season; continues to drop down the weights but she was never involved after a slow start at Newcastle last time and others are preferred.

RaceName: North Lakes Energy - Harry Doyle Memorial Maiden Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: Well treated on his best form for Seb Spencer but he's been out of sorts in his last four runs including when last of eight on stable debut at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) last month; overall record is now 0-10 and he needs a major revival.

RaceName: North Lakes Energy - Harry Doyle Memorial Maiden Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: Quirky maiden who virtually refused to race at Newcastle in February, but she ran well at Southwell on her penultimate run, and her best effort last season was a close call over C&D; returns after wind surgery and she's not ruled out back at this track.

RaceName: North Lakes Energy - Harry Doyle Memorial Maiden Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: Close second on debut at Dundalk (7f, AW) in January but he's been beaten 6l or more in all seven subsequent runs; left Robson De Aguiar for £5,500 last month; this is only his third handicap but he needs a transformation for new yard.

RaceName: North Lakes Energy - Harry Doyle Memorial Maiden Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: Lightly raced 5yo but he's not finished closer than 6l to a winner including in five handicaps; mark continues to fall but he has plenty to prove back in trip.

RaceName: North Lakes Energy - Harry Doyle Memorial Maiden Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: Big prices and he's struggled in three novice events including in two turf runs (1m, good to firm) this summer; still early days but he needs improvement back in trip on handicap debut.

RaceName: North Lakes Energy - Harry Doyle Memorial Maiden Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: Six-race maiden who has been well held in her last two starts but her standout effort was a strong-finishing second in a handicap here (6f, good) in June; has claims if she can recapture that form and this is only her second attempt at this trip.

RaceName: North Lakes Energy - Harry Doyle Memorial Maiden Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: 28-race maiden who has been tailed off in her last three starts and the latest was at this track (1m, good) last week; can only be watched.

RaceName: North Lakes Energy - Harry Doyle Memorial Maiden Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: 0-12 but he's reached the frame in five of his last six starts including when fourth of 13 in a classified event at Newcastle (6f, AW) last month; this return to 7f is no problem and he's a key player back in a handicap.

RaceName: North Lakes Energy - Harry Doyle Memorial Maiden Handicap (Div I)
Spotlight: No wins in 12 starts and he returned after a break with a laboured effort on his stable debut at Newcastle (6f, AW) last month; was a long way behind Long Shot in that race and he needs to bounce back near his best; cheekpieces reapplied.

RaceName: Juddmonte International Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: 5yo who showed career-best form to win the Group 1 Tattersalls Gold Cup at the Curragh (10.5f, good) in May on his reappearance; beaten just over 7l by Ombudsman when fourth in the Prince of Wales's Stakes at Royal Ascot (1m2f) where the fast ground may not have been ideal; today's surface is unlikely to be so quick and he's not ruled out each-way.

RaceName: Juddmonte International Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Listed runner-up at Kempton in April but he was a pacemaker for stablemate Ombudsman in the Prince of Wales's Stakes at Royal Ascot last time, when well beaten at 66-1, and that's set to be his role again.

RaceName: Juddmonte International Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Impressive in this race last year (good to firm) and took Group 1 tally to four with 4l win in the Prince of Wales's Stakes at Royal Ascot (1m2f, good to firm) in June last time; star 3yo Constitution River is a new rival but this fellow will be very tough to beat if producing his brilliant best.

RaceName: Juddmonte International Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: York has brought out the best in him, as evidenced by last season's Group 2 wins in the Dante (C&D, good to firm) and Great Voltigeur (1m4f, good to firm) and last month's second behind Item in the Group 2 York Stakes over C&D (good to firm); he may have been inconvenienced by making the running last time but has something to find back in a Group 1.

RaceName: Juddmonte International Stakes (Group 1)
OwnerName: His Highness The Aga Khans Studs S C
Spotlight: From the family of Arc winner Zarkava and this lightly raced 4yo made it five wins in a row with Group 3 success at Vichy (1m2f, soft) four weeks ago; has also won on good ground; this race is considerably hotter and others have a lot more substance to their form but he did it cosily last time and could still have lots more to offer for top French trainer who saddled Calandagan to finish second in this race in 2024 with the same silks; each-way possibilities.

RaceName: Juddmonte International Stakes (Group 1)
OwnerName: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier
Spotlight: Runner-up to Item in the Dante over C&D (good) in May but well beaten in Group 1s on his next three starts, having made the running each time; looks set for pacemaking duties once more; hard to fancy.

RaceName: Juddmonte International Stakes (Group 1)
OwnerName: M Tabor & D Smith & Mrs J Magnier & Westerberg
Spotlight: Runner-up on debut last July and 5-5 since, posting Group 1 wins on his last two starts in the Prix du Jockey Club at Chantilly (10.5f, good) and the Eclipse at Sandown (1m2f, good to firm); he's never faced a rival as good as Ombudsman but was impressive when winning the Eclipse by 3l and has the potential to give the Godolphin horse a serious challenge.

RaceName: Juddmonte International Stakes (Group 1)
OwnerName: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor
Spotlight: Won the Group 1 Futurity at Doncaster (1m, heavy) last October and reappeared with Group 3 win at Chantilly (1m1f, good to soft) in May; close second to Constitution River in the Group 1 Prix du Jockey Club at Chantilly (10.5f, good) next time, then beaten just over 3l by the same stablemate when third in the Eclipse at Sandown (1m2f, good to firm); has work to do but he could show improvement if settling better than on his last two starts.

RaceName: Juddmonte International Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Made it 3-3 when winning the Group 2 Dante over C&D (good) in May on reappearance and bounced back from soft-ground Derby flop to win the Group 2 York Stakes over C&D last month (good to firm; Pride Of Arras second); Ombudsman and fellow 3yo Constitution River have achieved more but his two course wins have come with something in hand and it's hard to identify where the ceiling of his ability lies, especially at York; entitled to respect.

RaceName: North Lakes Energy - Harry Doyle Memorial Maiden Handicap (Div II)
Spotlight: Nine-race maiden; not made a huge impact in handicaps this year, the latest off this mark at Ayr last week; others look stronger.

RaceName: North Lakes Energy - Harry Doyle Memorial Maiden Handicap (Div II)
Spotlight: 0-15 but he has shown winning potential, including when keeping on for fourth at Southwell on Sunday having been short of room over 1f out; has to prove his stamina for a stiff 7f though.

RaceName: North Lakes Energy - Harry Doyle Memorial Maiden Handicap (Div II)
Spotlight: Didn't progress for Andrew Balding and he hasn't offered a great deal in three runs for his new stable either; would have finished closer at Wolverhampton 19 days ago had he enjoyed a clear run but still looks vulnerable; drop in class a plus at least.

RaceName: North Lakes Energy - Harry Doyle Memorial Maiden Handicap (Div II)
Spotlight: Unexposed filly who wasn't beaten far when fifth of 11 on her handicap debut at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) 18 days ago; this stiffer track can help and she is open to improvement.

RaceName: North Lakes Energy - Harry Doyle Memorial Maiden Handicap (Div II)
Spotlight: 0-10 but he has finished second in three of his five runs this summer, the latest at Ripon (1m, good) 16 days ago; visor tried today (second in cheekpieces in June when headgear was tried once before); should be involved.

RaceName: North Lakes Energy - Harry Doyle Memorial Maiden Handicap (Div II)
Spotlight: Promising third in one run for Jamie Osborne as a 2yo (7f, AW); well beaten in three runs for Sam England, including when 50-1 for her handicap debut at Ripon 16 days ago; not easily recommended.

RaceName: North Lakes Energy - Harry Doyle Memorial Maiden Handicap (Div II)
Spotlight: Exposed maiden; runner-up in both 7f runs this year, the latest at Ayr last month; should give his running but may have to make do with more minor money.

RaceName: North Lakes Energy - Harry Doyle Memorial Maiden Handicap (Div II)
Spotlight: Modest maiden who wasn't at her best on AW over the winter; back from a break with cheekpieces left off.

RaceName: North Lakes Energy - Harry Doyle Memorial Maiden Handicap (Div II)
Spotlight: Not shown a great deal in six runs in sprint events, the latest 12 days ago; new trip/headgear not enough to tempt.

RaceName: Sky Bet Stayers Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
OwnerName: A Cope, B Roberts And J Biggane
Spotlight: Eight AW wins, two last winter in 2m handicaps; however, he has tons to prove on turf record (0-7) and even best AW form does not look good enough; reportedly lame after losing right-hind shoe when tailed off 19 days ago.

RaceName: Sky Bet Stayers Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 8yo whose 11th success came over 1m4f in April; also effective at 2m this term but edged back up the weights and looks vulnerable for win purposes.

RaceName: Sky Bet Stayers Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Ex-French 4yo who was upped to 2m on his third start for this yard when second of 20 in the Northumberland Plate at Newcastle (AW); smoothly went one better at Ascot (2m, good to firm) four weeks later, admittedly in just a four-runner race (from Ghaiyya and Fireblade) and that has earned him a 6lb rise, but he's relatively unexposed and heading the right way.

RaceName: Sky Bet Stayers Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Returned to Flat with an eye-catching effort at Royal Ascot (2m4f); going back down to 1m6f didn't look a problem at Glorious Goodwood (again good to firm) 18 days ago but he suffered a nightmare passage before running on into second of 13 (Valedictory fifth); a 4lb rise adds salt to the wounds but he could still have a big chance.

RaceName: Sky Bet Stayers Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Stepping up to 1m6f with cheekpieces enlisted resulted in wins at Goodwood (good) and Newmarket (good to firm); that's not ironed out all the kinks, though, as he looked hard work at Glorious Goodwood 18 days ago on his way to a fair fifth of 13, with Small Fry in second; probably needs to resume improvement on this first go at 2m but he's one to be reckoned with if first-time blinkers receive the same response that first-time cheekpieces did.

RaceName: Sky Bet Stayers Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Thorough Flat stayer who reappeared this spring with a career best on Flat to win at Navan (1m6f, heavy) and a creditable third in 3m hurdle race; good ground looked okay for him last season but a muted display at Royal Ascot nine weeks ago perhaps confirmed that anything firmer is not ideal; either way, another career best is needed today.

RaceName: Sky Bet Stayers Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Comes from off the pace; progressed very well initially this season; then wore cheekpieces on last two starts, never getting seriously involved as second favourite in the Northumberland Plate at Newcastle but beaten a nose by Shrimp Shady at Newbury (2m, good to firm); in the mix up 2lb.

RaceName: Sky Bet Stayers Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
OwnerName: Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum
Spotlight: Progressive in 2023, 2024 and 2025; that included getting pipped in the 2024 Cesarewitch (2m2f, soft) and two big runs last year at Goodwood; runner-up in his 2024 and 2025 reappearances, though not in such good races as this one; would have a lot more to prove on good to firm ground than good or softer, but this 2026 return is off a competitive mark.

RaceName: Sky Bet Stayers Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Only his second attempt over this far in a 31-race career came at Goodwood (soft) ten weeks ago when he came from the rear in a six-runner race to win by 5l; 6lb higher today (with more to prove if the ground is firmer than good) but new horizons as a stayer have been opened up.

RaceName: Sky Bet Stayers Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
OwnerName: Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum
Spotlight: 0-8 on turf; that's despite some good form last year but his best two runs this season were on AW, latterly when winning at Southwell early last month on his step up to 2m; that came by 13l in a five-runner race; has a 6lb higher mark in this very different contest but he's unexposed at the trip.

RaceName: Sky Bet Stayers Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Ex-Polish and German, placed in 1m2f Group races in 2024; took a while to find his level in Irish handicaps but decisively landed a gamble in a 24-runner race at the Curragh (1m6f, good) in May; should stay this far but never threatened at Royal Ascot (2m4f, sole start on officially good to firm) next time and weakened right out of it at Galway (2m1f) on latest, which leaves him with something to prove again.

RaceName: Sky Bet Stayers Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Won the 17-runner Chester Plate (2m2f, good) in May and beat Team Player by a nose to score at Newbury in July; another step forward when second in Shergar Cup race at Ascot (again 2m on good to firm) 11 days ago and a 1lb rise surely won't prevent another bold show.

RaceName: Sky Bet Stayers Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 1m4f Flat winner at last year's Galway festival and took a maiden hurdle this January; that's from 14 races for Donnacha O'Brien, for whom he was a promising third of 24 to Westminster Moon (1m6f, good) in May and a fair fifth over 2m in June; not beaten far when ninth in 2m Shergar Cup race at Ascot but that shows he needs marked improvement in today's first-time visor (1-8 in cheekpieces), replacing a tongue-tie.

RaceName: Sky Bet Stayers Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Unraced on softer than good; basically ran with credit in all her handicaps this term, winning one in April; however, no answers to Kirchner when second of four at Ascot (upped to 2m) last time and the handicapper might have her pegged.

RaceName: Sky Bet Stayers Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
OwnerName: Elb Bloodstock Ltd And R L Banks
Spotlight: Disappointed in this race last year and the form of his close third over C&D that September has not been matched; second of six at Ascot on penultimate start was his best show this term but he needs better than that.

RaceName: Sky Bet Stayers Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Maiden winner who was on the premises in all six handicaps, albeit managing only sixth of 20 when favourite for Northumberland Plate at Newcastle (upped to 2m) penultimate start on AW debut; on the heels of Shrimp Shady at Newbury latest; pretty reliable but needs to find extra for the win.

RaceName: Sky Bet Stayers Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Missed 2025; has mostly been coming from well off the pace this term and that yielded a win at Thirsk (2m, good) in May and he ended up on the heels of the leaders in a Shergar Cup race at Ascot (2m, good to firm) when next seen 11 days ago; 5lb claimer takes over in what looks a tougher race.

RaceName: David Allen IT Solutions Handicap
Spotlight: Dual Tapeta winner who won at Wolverhampton (6f, AW) for Jack Morland in April and was a close third there last month; now returns to turf for new yard but he ran some good races last summer including a close second at Doncaster (7f, good to soft); respected back in this sphere.

RaceName: David Allen IT Solutions Handicap
Spotlight: Group 3 winner in France as a 2yo but he's 0-13 since; yet to be placed in six runs for his current yard but he's on a reduced mark and made some eye-catching late headway at Musselburgh (7f, good) last time; should get a good tow into this race and he could be dangerous.

RaceName: David Allen IT Solutions Handicap
OwnerName: Mrs K S Pratt & M Dods
Spotlight: Five-time AW winner who completed a double when battling well at Southwell (7f) last month; record of 0-14 on turf but he has plenty of placed form in this sphere and is only 2lb higher than last time; could be a big factor again and any rain would be a bonus.

RaceName: David Allen IT Solutions Handicap
Spotlight: Versatile ground-wise and all four wins have been at 7f on turf; his mixed record this season but he wasn't beaten far at Ayr (1m) last time and is now only 1lb higher than for his last success; not ruled out back in trip.

RaceName: David Allen IT Solutions Handicap
Spotlight: Has run a number of good in defeat races this season and he got back on the scoresheet when justifying favouritism at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) last month; up 5lb but that was a comfortable success and he still looks feasibly treated; shortlisted.

RaceName: David Allen IT Solutions Handicap
Spotlight: His wins have come on slow ground but he was beaten only 3l in a big field at York (7f, good to firm) last month; that was a creditable effort after a slow start and he's a player if he can find some extra spark; stablemate of Misunderstood.

RaceName: David Allen IT Solutions Handicap
Spotlight: 0-22 since his Newbury maiden win in 2023 but he's on a reduced mark and ran well when sixth of 15 at York (1m, good to firm) last time; should get a good pace back in trip and has each-way claims if he gets the breaks.

RaceName: David Allen IT Solutions Handicap
Spotlight: Added to his 2yo novice win when making all to justify support at Musselburgh (7f, good) in June; this is a deeper race but a 3lb rise looks fair and he's well drawn to attack; respected.

RaceName: David Allen IT Solutions Handicap
Spotlight: Five wins this year, with first four on AW and latest on turf at Redcar (7f, good) in May; placed twice since that last success but he didn't shine at Doncaster last time and he looks weighted near best off this mark.

RaceName: David Allen IT Solutions Handicap
Spotlight: Got back on the scoresheet with a 20-1 win at Newcastle (7f, AW) in March; didn't get any luck at York next time but he was well held on his return visit at the end of May; has bit to prove again after a break but he's only 1lb higher than for his last win.

RaceName: David Allen IT Solutions Handicap
Spotlight: Dual winner since a visor was added in February and he ran another good race when a close fifth of 18 at York (7f, good to firm) last month; 1lb lower here and he should be in the thick of things again.

RaceName: David Allen IT Solutions Handicap
Spotlight: First three wins were on turf but last three have come on Tapeta; only 1lb higher than for his Wolverhampton win in January but that was a Class 5 and he finished out the back in his final run during the winter; now goes back up in grade and he has work to do after 189 days off.

RaceName: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Prominent racer who won competitive 5f races at Epsom, York and Glorious Goodwood on her last three handicap starts (good/good to firm); she's 8lb higher than last time but did it in convincing fashion; strong claims.

RaceName: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: 2yo campaign concluded with good third in Doncaster sales race (6.5f, good to soft); just one start this year, when keeping on strongly for close Listed third at Sandown (5f, good) in June; this sharp 5f may not play to his strengths but he has a Group 1 entry and is one to be interested in.

RaceName: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: C&D Listed winner (good to firm) at this meeting last August and she followed up in the Group 2 Flying Childers at Doncaster (5f, good); on a handy mark on that form but she's been a long way below that level this year.

RaceName: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Front-runner who was sixth of 18 to Naana's Shadow at Glorious Goodwood (5f, good to firm) and has been placed at Pontefract either side of that (5f, good to firm; most recently on Sunday); back into a more competitive race today but this track should suit his style and he has an each-way chance.

RaceName: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Won at Redcar (5f, good) in June and short-headed by Naana's Shadow over this C&D (good) seven days later; not beaten far when sixth then fifth in big fields at Ascot (5f, good to firm) and Goodwood (5f, good to firm) on his last two starts; in with an each-way shout.

RaceName: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Made debut in April and has run really well behind Naana's Shadow in his two handicaps, finishing third of 13 over C&D (good) then fourth of 18 at Goodwood (5f, good to firm); there's every chance that he will be in the mix in a first-time tongue-tie.

RaceName: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Won on reappearance at Sandown (5f, good) in April and denied a clear run when Listed sixth over this C&D (good) next time; soundly beaten in Royal Ascot handicap latest but, with the Sandown form having been strongly franked by the placed horses, he's not written off; a tongue-tie goes on.

RaceName: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Respectable seventh on stable debut in the 5f 3yo handicap at Royal Ascot (good to firm) and good third of 18 to Naana's Shadow at Glorious Goodwood (5f, good to firm) three weeks ago; today's track should be a good fit for this front-runner and she could make a bold bid.

RaceName: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Won two in a row at Hamilton (6f, good to firm) and Chester (5f, good to soft) before midfield finish at Royal Ascot (5f, good to firm) and runner-up to an odds-on winner at Chester (6f, good) last time; he's particularly effective at Chester but is not ruled out each-way on his first run here.

RaceName: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Third on debut at Newcastle (7f, AW) in February and he won AW novice races at Kempton (6f) and Newcastle (5f) on his next two starts; makes handicap debut in a hot contest after three months off but his stable is in fine form and he certainly brings potential; one to consider.

RaceName: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Second of 17 off this mark on reappearance over C&D (good) in May; however, she hasn't threatened since and, while there have been possible excuses, she now needs to turn things around in a first-time visor.

RaceName: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Front-runner who won two in a row in the first half of summer (5f, good) but he finished down the field at Glorious Goodwood (5f, good to firm) and it was the same story at Pontefract (5f, good to firm) on Sunday.

RaceName: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Slowly away and unplaced on his two outings this season; however, he was strong in the betting for both and it's possible he'll be sharper today in the first-time visor; interesting to see if his backers return.

RaceName: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Won in April on first two starts, then made the frame in two competitive handicaps (5f, good; including here) before creditable Listed fifth at Ayr (5f, soft); she's better than she showed at Goodwood three weeks ago, when minus the hood and failing to settle, but the hood is again left off.

RaceName: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: He had started to become disappointing but returned to form with a close fourth at 100-1 at Ascot (5f, good to firm) last month on his second stable start; he'd have been closer with a clear run and could be in the shake-up if he gets the breaks.

RaceName: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Won at Musselburgh (5f, good) in June and did well to finish third at Newmarket (5f, good to firm) last month having been hampered early; however, he was only fifth of 13 over this C&D in between those runs and was disappointing at Musselburgh on latest outing; others are more compelling.

RaceName: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Made all on handicap debut at Pontefract (5f, good) in June and bounced back from lesser run on soft going at Chester when going very close here (5.4f, good to firm) last time; up in grade today but she came well clear with the winner last time and return to a bare 5f could suit this speedy filly.

RaceName: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Listed runner-up here last October and he's well treated on that form but he's been a long way below that level on his six outings this season (three of them here); a major turnaround is necessary.

RaceName: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
Spotlight: Highly capable on her day, as when going close in the 3yo Dash at Epsom (5f, good) in June; a case can be made on that form but this headstrong filly has been well beaten on both starts since and has something to prove.

OwnerName: In For A Penny Partnership & Partner
Spotlight: Made the breakthrough when making all in a Redcar handicap (7f, good) in May; mixed form in four subsequent runs, but he went close at Leicester (6f, good to firm; cheekpieces added) last month and had an excuse at Thirsk (stumbled at the start) last time; still unexposed at this trip and he's a big player if he can recapture his penultimate form.

RaceName: Armstrong Watson Handicap
Spotlight: Sole win was in a small-field novice at Musselburgh (5f, soft) last autumn but she's on a reduced mark and was an eye-catching second at Thirsk (6f, good) 12 days ago; should go well again and it would be a positive if rain arrives.

RaceName: Armstrong Watson Handicap
Spotlight: Showed some promise in four runs for Donnacha O'Brien this season including when fourth of 15 in a Cork maiden (6f, soft) in May; never dangerous in a Curragh handicap in June but it's still early days and she needs watching in market on stable debut (changed hands for 14,000gns).

RaceName: Armstrong Watson Handicap
Spotlight: Signed off for Edward Bethell with a good second at Redcar (6f, good) in June but she's not come close to that form in three runs for her current yard; on same mark as for her fifth here (7f, good) last week and she has plenty to prove.

RaceName: Armstrong Watson Handicap
Spotlight: Made the most of a favourable draw, running down the pacesetter at Redcar (6f, good) in June; down the field in both subsequent runs, but he looked stretched over 7f at Doncaster last time and is now only 3lb higher than for his win; could be dangerous back in trip.

RaceName: Armstrong Watson Handicap
Spotlight: Struggled in his three qualifying runs and same story when eighth of ten on handicap debut at Newcastle (7f, AW) last month; still early days but he needs a transformation on this switch to sprinting.

RaceName: Armstrong Watson Handicap
OwnerName: Ursa Major Racing Ltd And M Dods
Spotlight: Raced prominently when a creditable third in a Ripon handicap (6f, good) in May but he's been well held in three runs since; record is now 0-9 and he needs to get back on track after wind surgery.

RaceName: Armstrong Watson Handicap
Spotlight: Started this year with a second at Newcastle (6f, AW) in February but he's lost his way in last three starts including a heavy defeat here (7f, good) in May; resumes off a reduced mark but he needs a big turnaround with blinkers added.

RaceName: CopyBet Bog Now For York Tomorrow Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Made all at Fontwell (2m5f, good) in May when back over hurdles and runner-up at Uttoxeter (2m7f, good) since; she can make mistakes and fell on her last chase start in December, but won over fences at Cheltenham (3m1f, good to soft) previously; respected under regular rider Lily Bradstock.

RaceName: CopyBet Bog Now For York Tomorrow Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Returned to form in a reapplied tongue-tie (retained since) and justified strong market support at Bangor (2m4f, good) in March; mixed form since, however, and only fifth at Uttoxeter (2m4f, good) last month following a break and wind surgery; needs to raise his game and is unproven at the trip.

RaceName: CopyBet Bog Now For York Tomorrow Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Point/hunter chase winner who went close over hurdles on first two starts for this yard before handicap chase win at Newton Abbot (3m2f, good to firm) last month; did it nicely last time and a 5lb rise may well not stop him.

RaceName: CopyBet Bog Now For York Tomorrow Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Back to form with 9l second to well-handicapped winner at Market Rasen (extended 2m5f, good) in June and it was the competitive Summer Plate there in which he was soundly beaten last time (hampered four out and wasn't disgraced); could be in the mix back down in grade, provided the step back up in trip isn't an issue; wears first-time blinkers.

RaceName: CopyBet Bog Now For York Tomorrow Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Good second over C&D (good) last September and ran pretty well in fourth over C&D (good) four weeks ago, when she was hampered three out on her second start back from a break; wears first-time cheekpieces and could get closer to the target this afternoon.

RaceName: CopyBet Bog Now For York Tomorrow Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: He's on a reduced mark and has been in pretty good heart since these blinkers went on; however, he needs something extra if he's to post a first win since March 2025, and a longer trip is probably preference.

RaceName: Sligo Plumb Centre Mares Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Off the mark at the third attempt in bumpers in Fairyhouse Listed in April; hurdles debut run at Kilbeggan last month was okay, early this month still in contention when faller three out in 2m1f Cork mares' maiden; remains capable of better, providing she avoids serious error.

RaceName: Sligo Plumb Centre Mares Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Has shown a decent level of ability in three bumpers since May (all on good), runner-up at Tramore and Wexford before readily landing 2m1f contest at latter venue last month, sent on some way out and clear in straight for 7l win; half-sister to a couple of hurdles winners and out of a half-sister to Stayers' Hurdle winner Big Bucks, so certainly bred for this; likely the one to beat.

RaceName: Sligo Plumb Centre Mares Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Modest Flat winner is 0-6 hurdling although improvement of late, finishing a decent fourth of 20 in 2m1f Galway handicap and chased home a ready winner in 7-runner 2m2f Downpatrick mares' maiden, both on good ground; place prospects again.

RaceName: Sligo Plumb Centre Mares Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Solid fourth in 2m Clonmel maiden on debut in May but didn't appear to stay 2m4f at Limerick; switched to bumpers both starts at this venue, placed on first occasion; good bit more needed back in a maiden, eligible for a mark after this.

RaceName: Sligo Plumb Centre Mares Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Poet's Word half-sister to useful 2m5f chase/3m hurdle winner Nelson County; dam well held in 2m2f/2m4f hurdles, closely related to Irish Grand National winner Our Duke; debutante worth a market check although bred to want further.

RaceName: Sligo Plumb Centre Mares Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Point-to-point winner last November but three hurdling efforts have been modest; easily passed over.

RaceName: Sligo Plumb Centre Mares Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Poor sort on the Flat and never sighted on recent hurdles debut in C&D maiden.

RaceName: Sligo Plumb Centre Mares Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Pulled up in a pair of point-to-points last October and tailed off last of 7 on recent hurdles debut at Downpatrick.

RaceName: Sligo Plumb Centre Mares Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Poor efforts in recent maidens at Cork and over C&D.

RaceName: Sky Bet Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: 550,000gns breeze-up buy who comfortably beat Crystal Queen and one other to win at Ayr (5f, good to firm) on his debut in May; just 13-2 and 15-2 when held in two subsequent Group-race assignments and he still carries plenty of potential into this first taste of handicaps.

RaceName: Sky Bet Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Green on debut but hasn't looked back since and, having forced a dead-heat in 6f Newmarket Listed race, she completed a hat-trick on her handicap debut over that C&D (also good to firm) 18 days ago; she was being considered for tomorrow's Group 2 Lowther and warrants close inspection.

RaceName: Sky Bet Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: All three runs at 5f on good to firm; second to Ruler's Pride on debut at Ayr in May and showed the benefit of that experience when nicely on top in Beverley's Hilary Needler just ten days later; far from disgraced when beaten 6l (fifth in group) in good renewal of the Queen Mary at Royal Ascot the following month; off since but she shaped last time as if she's worth a go at 6f and she is one to consider on her nursery debut.

RaceName: Sky Bet Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Created a good impression when winning on his debut at Newbury (6f, good) in May; well beaten in the Coventry at Royal Ascot next time but didn't run badly in a Listed event back at Newbury last month; has since left James Ferguson and is tongue tied for this stable/nursery debut.

RaceName: Sky Bet Nursery Handicap
OwnerName: Future Champions Racing Syn & Mps Racing
Spotlight: Comfortably off the mark at Hamilton (5f, good to soft) in June and he may have been unfortunate (drifted right) when nailed close home on his nursery debut at Glorious Goodwood (6f, good to firm) 19 days ago; up 4lb but Ryan Moore retains the ride and the partnership should be thereabouts.

RaceName: Sky Bet Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: A really encouraging debut under Colin Keane at Leicester (6f, good to firm) in May when chasing home the subsequent Albany winner but hasn't come close to matching that form in two subsequent outings, latterly when beaten a long way in Goodwood maiden three weeks ago; hopes pinned on fresh blinkers, a gelding operation and the returning Keane on this handicap debut.

RaceName: Sky Bet Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Stayed on well to win C&D novice (good) at the Dante meeting in May and didn't get the chance to show what he could do in Royal Ascot's Norfolk the following month; better than the bare result when 5l adrift of Dubai Champion at Goodwood last time; not without a chance.

RaceName: Sky Bet Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Bath novice winner (5f, firm) who handled the step up to 6f well when fourth of 18 in Goodwood nursery (good to firm; Dubai Champion second) 19 days ago; considered.

RaceName: Sky Bet Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Looked good when taking a Sandown novice (5f, good) in June but safely held in better events subsequently, a 6f Listed event last time; handicap debut.

RaceName: Sky Bet Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: 6f Doncaster novice winner last month who made a solid handicap debut when second of five there (6.5f, again good to firm) three weeks later; this is much more competitive, however, and he's up 3lb; cheekpieces go on.

RaceName: Sky Bet Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Made most when taking a Yarmouth novice (6f, good) on his debut in May but came up short in a useful Ascot event last month; has been gelded and he's the least exposed of these; handicap debut.

RaceName: Sky Bet Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Shaped nicely when second over C&D (good to firm) on her debut last month and she coped well with the drop to 5f when bagging a Sandown maiden (good) a fortnight ago; solid run when fifth of 13 in 5f Newbury Listed event last Friday; makes a quick return back at 6f for this handicap debut.

RaceName: Sky Bet Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Good-ground Chester novice winner but he was only fourth of seven under a penalty at Ripon (also 6f, good to firm) three weeks ago; opening mark looks punchy on that evidence but it's still early days.

RaceName: Sky Bet Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Showed a good level in his qualifying runs but was only seventh of 18 when favourite for Goodwood nursery (6f, good to firm; Dubai Champion, Sovereign Glory and Super Tuscan ahead) last time; reportedly hung that day, so maybe today's cheekpieces will keep his mind on the job; Oisin Murphy retains the ride.

RaceName: Sky Bet Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Brocklesby fifth who has shown improved and consistent form in four subsequent outings, including when off the mark in Southwell novice (6f, AW) four weeks ago; probably needs more on this nursery debut but that's not inconceivable.

RaceName: Sky Bet Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: He had gone fairly close in two maidens before coming good when upped in trip and making all at Hamilton (6f, good) 18 days ago; this opening mark looks quite tempting based on that and he commands attention.

RaceName: Sky Bet Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: He scored on his third start when taking Chepstow novice in June and it was a creditable sixth of 18 in Goodwood nursery (also 6f, good to firm; Dubai Champion and Sovereign Glory ahead) last time; will need to better that, though.

RaceName: Sky Bet Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: He was just pegged back in Windsor novice (6f) last month and beaten only a length at Yarmouth (7f, again good to firm) three weeks ago; the drop back to 6f should suit but his opening mark demands a bigger effort.

RaceName: Sky Bet Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: His third of six here (5f, good) was a fairly encouraging debut effort but it's been downhill since, including when last of 14 over this trip on AW last time; new cheekpieces will need to help him tap back into that initial promise.

RaceName: Sky Bet Nursery Handicap
OwnerName: N Bradley Racing 29, D Scott & P Spencer
Spotlight: She took a big step forward from her introduction when comfortably winning a six-runner Musselburgh maiden (5f, good) in June; similar form when fourth of six in C&D novice (good to firm) last month and she's not readily dismissed on this first go in a handicap.

RaceName: Sky Bet Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: All three of his starts have been on good ground over C&D; promising sixth behind Persian Spring on  debut in May was built on when beaten less than 3l in a maiden one month later; didn't match that when down the field a fortnight on, however, and was subsequently gelded; handicap debut.

RaceName: Sky Bet Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: He was beaten 18l on his debut in March's Brocklesby but showed dramatic improvement to bag Beverley maiden (5f, good to soft) at 25-1 for Stephen Hanlon in May; proved that was no fluke when a big-priced second on nursery debut over C&D for Noel Wilson last month and won at Hamilton (6f, good to firm) just six days later; up 5lb in a much tougher race but he's worth a look; stable debut.

RaceName: Unibet Interactive Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 45,000gns yearling; gelding by Oasis Dream; half-brother to 6f winner Magical Merlin (including 2yo; RPR 88); dam unplaced 1m 2yo (51), half-sister to Listed winners Choose Me (7.4f; dam of Group 1 winners Persuasive and Creative Force) and Shanghai Glory (6f); watch the betting on debut.

RaceName: Unibet Interactive Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Frankel colt; second foal; dam 6f 2yo winner (including Group 1 Prix Morny; RPR 115), half-sister to Listed-placed 1m4f winner Climate Friendly, out of unraced half-sister to US 1m1f Grade 3 winner Gender Agenda, family of Oaks/St Leger winner User Friendly; has a smart pedigree and he's interesting on his debut.

RaceName: Unibet Interactive Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 14,000gns 3yo; gelding by Kingman; sixth foal; brother to 7f-1m1f winner Nikovo (including AW; RPR 99), half-brother to winners Dantora (1m2f; 89), Donna Nook (7f AW 2yo/1m turf; 87) and Tremaine (French 1m1f 2yo); dam 7f-1m1f winner (including 2yo/Listed; 102); his stable can ready a newcomer and he's one to keep an eye on in the betting.

RaceName: Unibet Interactive Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Shaped with promise despite greenness when fifth of eight on his debut at Ffos Las (1m, good) in June but went backwards from that effort over that same C&D two weeks ago; drops to 7f for his AW debut.

RaceName: Unibet Interactive Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Down the field on her debut at Saint-Cloud (6.5f, very soft) last September but she's finished fourth and sixth there in two starts this year (7f/1m), the most recent coming in April; has since left Andre Fabre having been bought for 12,000gns and she's interesting on her stable/AW debut.

RaceName: Unibet Interactive Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
OwnerName: Hot To Trot Racing And R Mitchell
Spotlight: 0-4 but she was beaten only 3l when third of 11 on her debut over this C&D last December, and posted an improved effort when narrowly denied on her handicap debut at Wolverhampton (7f, AW) 19 days ago; returns to a maiden with solid claims.

RaceName: Unibet Interactive Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Half-sister to 6f/7f winner Dubai Treasure (including AW/Listed; RPR 112); sent off 9-2 on her debut at Sandown (7f, soft) last August but she didn't see it out having been caught wide; off since but her half-sister is 2-2 on the AW and the market should be informative on her reappearance.

RaceName: Unibet Interactive Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Showed little when last of five on her debut at Yarmouth (7f, good to firm; 40-1) last month and a big step forward will be required on her AW debut.

RaceName: Unibet Interactive Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Runner-up to a subsequent Group 2 winner on her debut at Nottingham (8.5f, good) in April and ran to a similar level at Wolverhampton (8.5f) next time; off since a solid third of ten at Windsor (1m, good) in May and now drops to 7f on her return to the AW; contender.

RaceName: Knights Handicap
Spotlight: Won on turf (1m, good to soft) three years ago but his three wins since have come on AW; up 7lb for his easy front-running success at Wolverhampton (8.6f) three weeks ago; thriving and commands respect.

RaceName: Knights Handicap
Spotlight: C&D winner; on a losing run but he has run several good races in defeat this year, including here; more minor money on the cards.

RaceName: Knights Handicap
Spotlight: Placed in his first two handicaps and he made no mistake back from a break at Ayr (1m, good to soft) nine days ago; the forecast rain won't hurt his chance and he still has time on his side; one to be interested in under a penalty.

RaceName: Knights Handicap
Spotlight: Prominent racer; made all at Southwell (1m) in April; some fair runs in defeat since but he could face competition for the lead and others are more appealing for win purposes.

RaceName: Knights Handicap
Spotlight: Took a while to put his head in front but he is thriving now, winning a C&D handicap in June and adding an apprentice handicap over C&D (for Conor Whiteley) last week; unpenalised today and has plenty in his favour.

RaceName: Knights Handicap
OwnerName: Middleham Park Racing Lxvi And P Demilow
Spotlight: 2-5 in handicaps this season, coming from off the pace to win at Redcar (1m, good to firm) in April and adding an 8.3f success at Hamilton 18 days ago; 3lb higher today and doesn't have the benefit of Conor Whiteley's claim but he is still low mileage and could progress further.

RaceName: Knights Handicap
Spotlight: C&D win (soft) in June off a 2lb lower mark; solid efforts in defeat since and the forecast rain won't be a problem; still needs the new headgear to squeeze out a bit more.

RaceName: Knights Handicap
Spotlight: Chased home Ravishing Beauty here (soft) in June; 1lb lower today but that run has been followed by two disappointing efforts; the more rain to fall the better.

RaceName: Knights Handicap
Spotlight: 1m AW winner for Harry Charlton in December; sold for 22,000gns in April; low-key stable debut last week and hard to recommend on the back of that.

RaceName: CopyBet Pay First Past The Post Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Did well for Tom Lacey in early part of last season, winning three times over hurdles, and reappeared with fairly encouraging chase debut in May; failed to build on that when well-held fourth over C&D last month but still enters calculations in this lower grade.

RaceName: CopyBet Pay First Past The Post Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Went very close off today's mark on chasing debut at Stratford (2m1f, good to firm; form has worked out well) in May, after a layoff; major player if judged on that effort but finished rather weakly on both subsequent outings and is now 0-21 under all codes.

RaceName: CopyBet Pay First Past The Post Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
OwnerName: G C Myddelton & V E C Taylor
Spotlight: Needs to rebound from last month's poor hurdle run but was second in two good-ground C&D chases last summer (including this race) and has slipped to a good mark; will be dangerous if back on song in first-time cheekpieces.

RaceName: CopyBet Pay First Past The Post Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Free-going front-runner; just 1-14 over hurdles but was seemingly back in good form when placed at Uttoxeter (2m, good) last month; could take some catching if he gets into a good jumping rhythm on chasing debut.

RaceName: CopyBet Pay First Past The Post Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Now 1lb lower than when winning at Cartmel (2m1f, good) last summer but has not been at his best this season, and was behind Getaway Jewel when fourth at Cartmel last month; needs to up his game.

RaceName: CopyBet Pay First Past The Post Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Caused 28-1 surprise over C&D (good) on chase debut in June and bounced back from lesser effort when third over 2m4f here (good) last month; remains lightly raced and this drop back in trip looks the right move; respected.

RaceName: CopyBet Pay First Past The Post Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: 2-11 over hurdles, the latter win gained from the front at Fontwell (2m3f, good) in April; not quite in same form when dropped back to 2m1f there in May and makes chase debut after three-month break but could have a say.

RaceName: CopyBet Pay First Past The Post Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Ex-Irish 8yo; didn't get home after racing too freely over 3m on stable debut in June but was evidently well suited by drop to about 2m2f (if additional yardage is included) when scoring at Market Rasen (good) last month; could easily have more to offer for new yard; must be considered.

RaceName: CopyBet Pay First Past The Post Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Unplaced in all seven Irish points this year and made low-key return to racing under rules when well beaten here (2m4f, good) on last month's stable debut; drops back in trip with cheekpieces tried today.

RaceName: CopyBet Pay First Past The Post Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Four-time chase winner who has made the frame on all four starts since returning from a break in May, most recently when second at Cartmel (2m1f, good) last month; has his limitations and is not getting any younger but ought to give another good account.

RaceName: Aidan Moffitt Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Flashes of form over hurdles and fences during a light campaign in 2025; produced a bright display when second to the improving Koeur A Prendre at Ballinrobe last week, on his first outing since March.

RaceName: Aidan Moffitt Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Two Flat wins in 2024; unplaced in three Flat handicaps last month; not disgraced when set a very stiff task in a Galway novice hurdle; down the field in a Flat handicap last week; relatively unexposed over hurdles.

RaceName: Aidan Moffitt Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: One fair run on the Flat in Britain; weak maiden hurdle form; pulled up on handicap debut at Cork; respect for local yard is the only positive.

RaceName: Aidan Moffitt Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Faced a tough task in a maiden at the Galway festival; worth considering on a fair handicap run at Roscommon (beaten around 12l in third), but that was over 3m; hard to be sure if this trip will bring out the best in him; tongue-tie added.

RaceName: Aidan Moffitt Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Gained his sole hurdles success in this event in 2024; unconvincing Flat form this summer makes him hard to fancy; however, he showed fair form over hurdles in the first half of 2025.

RaceName: Aidan Moffitt Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Inconsistent sort; won off 7lb lower here in May; down the field on her next two starts; a clear second, 11l in front of today's rival Granlahan, at Kilbeggan on penultimate start; failed to reproduce that form at the same venue two weeks later.

RaceName: Aidan Moffitt Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Won twice in Britain early in his career; was off for a long time; weak Irish form on the Flat and over hurdles since his return; in rear on the Flat at Gowran last week; mid-division at Cork on his most recent hurdles start; new headgear combination

RaceName: Aidan Moffitt Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Only one win from 27 starts over hurdles, at Ballinrobe last year off 13lb higher (2m6f, good); badly out of form in four outings this season, three of them at this venue.

RaceName: Aidan Moffitt Memorial Handicap Hurdle
OwnerName: Miss Phidelma Elvin & Donal P Keane
Spotlight: Weak form in maidens; cheekpieces failed to produce any improvement when pulled up at Limerick in May on handicap debut; blinkers tried now.

RaceName: Aidan Moffitt Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Weak form in maidens; absent since tailed off on handicap debut at Clonmel last December; trainer saddled a winner at this venue early this month.

RaceName: Aidan Moffitt Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Placed four times over hurdles; third over C&D in June and at Kilbeggan last month, though he was more than 10l behind runner-up Bowgate Street on that occasion; appeared not to stay 2m6f at Ballinrobe; beaten 12l by an unchallenged front-runner when second at Downpatrick; a likely player in a race of modest standard; stable in form.

RaceName: Aidan Moffitt Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Won 2m Thurles handicap in March 2025 for Aengus King; inconsistent before and after that long-priced success; attracted some support at Wexford last month on her stable debut, faded after stumbling three out; some merit in her run at Cork early in the month.

RaceName: Aidan Moffitt Memorial Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Showed next to nothing in maidens; has struggled in three handicaps; 25-1 when pulled up at Wexford 12 days ago; hard to make a case.

RaceName: Unibet 3 Uniboosts A Day Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Eighth of ten on his debut at Newbury (6f, good) in May and hasn't built on that in two starts since; has been given wind surgery since last seen two months ago and steps back up in trip on his nursery/AW debut; may do better.

RaceName: Unibet 3 Uniboosts A Day Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Hinted at ability when fifth on his debut at Salisbury (6f, soft) in June; ran below that level on quick ground at Doncaster next time and beat only one home in a conditions event at Ascot (6f, good to firm) last month; has since been gelded and steps up to 7f for his nursery/AW debut (dam won on the AW) with the hood removed.

RaceName: Unibet 3 Uniboosts A Day Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Failed to beat a rival home on her first two starts for this trainer but she was a solid third of ten here over 6f on her nursery debut two weeks ago; has enough in her pedigree to suggest she'll stay this longer trip and has claims.

RaceName: Unibet 3 Uniboosts A Day Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Tongue-tied for all three starts, including when sixth of ten in a nursery here over 6f two weeks ago (behind Kochella); left the impression he could be suited by this longer trip on that occasion and makes some appeal despite being drawn widest.

RaceName: Unibet 3 Uniboosts A Day Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Best effort from three starts when third of ten in a novice over this C&D in June (beaten around 6l) but he was disappointing at Catterick (7f, good to firm) four weeks ago; switches back to the AW for his nursery debut.

RaceName: Unibet 3 Uniboosts A Day Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Runner-up in a seller at Chester (7f, good to soft) and novice at Chepstow (6f, good to firm) in June; however, he's been well held in both starts since, including on his nursery debut at Ffos Las (7.5f, good) three weeks ago; others preferred.

RaceName: Unibet 3 Uniboosts A Day Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Shaped well when fourth of nine on her debut at Chepstow (5f, soft) in June but she hasn't built on that in two starts since (both on good to firm), including in a first-time hood there last month; steps up in trip for her nursery debut with better needed.

RaceName: Unibet 3 Uniboosts A Day Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Hung right when ninth of 13 at Newbury (6f, good to firm) on her second start and she failed to beat a rival home at Ascot (6f, good to firm) last month; steps up in trip for her AW/nursery debut.

RaceName: Unibet 3 Uniboosts A Day Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Ran his best race when fifth of seven at Chepstow (7f, good to firm) last month but he was down the field on his nursery debut at Ffos Las (7.5f, good) three weeks ago; now switches to the AW having been dropped 2lb.

RaceName: Unibet 3 Uniboosts A Day Nursery Handicap
OwnerName: Hold My Beer, N Bradley 6, L Bearman
Spotlight: Modest form in three starts in maiden/novice company (6f/7f) but he was sent off favourite on his debut at Windsor in May; has been gelded since last seen 49 days ago and switches to the AW with a tongue-tie/blinkers applied; open to progress on his nursery debut.

RaceName: Unibet 3 Uniboosts A Day Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Down the field in each of her three starts (7f; good to firm), most recently when fading into eighth of nine at Epsom 20 days ago; makes her AW and nursery debut with cheekpieces added.

RaceName: Unibet 3 Uniboosts A Day Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: No better than seventh on her first three starts over 5f and fared no better when eighth of ten on her nursery debut at Leicester (7f, good to firm; beaten 18l) last month; dropped 3lb and now makes her AW debut.

RaceName: Unibet 3 Uniboosts A Day Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Beaten at least 11l in each of his first three starts and wasn't able to improve on his nursery debut at Chepstow (6f, good to firm; first-time blinkers; gelded) last month; this longer trip needs to bring about some improvement.

RaceName: CopyBet Support Safer Gambling Mares' Maiden Hurdle (ARC Summer Novices' Brush Hdl Qualifier) (GBB)
Spotlight: Point winner who came good under rules at second attempt, with clear success in five-runner Sedgefield bumper (good) in October; had excuse (bled from the nose) when pulled up there on hurdling debut in November but we haven't seen her since.

RaceName: CopyBet Support Safer Gambling Mares' Maiden Hurdle (ARC Summer Novices' Brush Hdl Qualifier) (GBB)
Spotlight: Displayed improvement in her third bumper, winning by over 6l at Kelso (good) in May; it's tricky to gauge what that form is worth but she should have a future over jumps.

RaceName: CopyBet Support Safer Gambling Mares' Maiden Hurdle (ARC Summer Novices' Brush Hdl Qualifier) (GBB)
Spotlight: Well beaten in good-ground Bangor bumper in May, after a long absence, and needs significant improvement on this hurdling debut.

RaceName: CopyBet Support Safer Gambling Mares' Maiden Hurdle (ARC Summer Novices' Brush Hdl Qualifier) (GBB)
Spotlight: Displayed minor promise in all three bumpers, most recently when sixth of 12 (about 12l behind Sparkling Water) at Uttoxeter (good) last month; more will be required on this hurdling debut, though.

RaceName: CopyBet Support Safer Gambling Mares' Maiden Hurdle (ARC Summer Novices' Brush Hdl Qualifier) (GBB)
Spotlight: Left behind by ready winner when second at Newton Abbot (2m1f, good; first-time cheekpieces) last month but has now made the frame on all four hurdling starts; ought to act as a good benchmark here.

RaceName: CopyBet Support Safer Gambling Mares' Maiden Hurdle (ARC Summer Novices' Brush Hdl Qualifier) (GBB)
Spotlight: Out of a half-sister to useful jumper Bobs Law; beaten about 18l when sixth of 14 in course bumper in June; probably best watched on hurdle debut.

RaceName: CopyBet Support Safer Gambling Mares' Maiden Hurdle (ARC Summer Novices' Brush Hdl Qualifier) (GBB)
Spotlight: Pulled up in heavy-ground Limerick claiming hurdle on latest rules start in February but won two British points in May and has possibilities here if able to replicate the best of last year's Irish form.

RaceName: CopyBet Support Safer Gambling Mares' Maiden Hurdle (ARC Summer Novices' Brush Hdl Qualifier) (GBB)
Spotlight: Runner-up in three bumpers in 2024 but her Flat win in June came in a basement-grade classified race and she'll need to take pretty well to hurdling to pose a threat here.

RaceName: CopyBet Support Safer Gambling Mares' Maiden Hurdle (ARC Summer Novices' Brush Hdl Qualifier) (GBB)
Spotlight: Delivered on promise shown for Ralph Beckett during the winter when winning good-ground Uttoxeter bumper for new stable last month; ought to play another major role on this hurdling debut.

RaceName: CopyBet Support Safer Gambling Mares' Maiden Hurdle (ARC Summer Novices' Brush Hdl Qualifier) (GBB)
Spotlight: Won a point bumper in 2023 and came third in two 2m3f hurdle races towards end of that year but returned from long absence with two underwhelming runs last winter and has been off for another seven months since.

RaceName: CopyBet Support Safer Gambling Mares' Maiden Hurdle (ARC Summer Novices' Brush Hdl Qualifier) (GBB)
Spotlight: Struggled in two course bumpers when owner-trained in June 2025; makes stable/hurdle debut after 420-day absence.

RaceName: CopyBet Support Safer Gambling Mares' Maiden Hurdle (ARC Summer Novices' Brush Hdl Qualifier) (GBB)
Spotlight: Out of a half-sister to stable's Cheltenham Gold Cup winner Coneygree and high-class jumper Carruthers but finished well down the field in a course bumper on debut in June.

RaceName: CopyBet Support Safer Gambling Mares' Maiden Hurdle (ARC Summer Novices' Brush Hdl Qualifier) (GBB)
Spotlight: Unseated rider at first flight on hurdle debut in June and did not get seriously competitive in two subsequent Uttoxeter novices (both 2m, good).

RaceName: CopyBet Support Safer Gambling Mares' Maiden Hurdle (ARC Summer Novices' Brush Hdl Qualifier) (GBB)
OwnerName: Posh Pundit Racing Club & G Nicholls
Spotlight: Fair Flat racer at up to 1m6f with 4-22 strike-rate; placed on all three hurdling starts, most recently when third at Newton Abbot (2m1f, good to soft) last month, and has good each-way claims again.

RaceName: CopyBet Support Safer Gambling Mares' Maiden Hurdle (ARC Summer Novices' Brush Hdl Qualifier) (GBB)
Spotlight: Showed some ability during five-race Flat career for Ralph Beckett but was in rear throughout (ride attracted stewards' attention) when making hurdling debut against own age-group last month.

RaceName: Solar Generation Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Five Flat wins in Britain, at up to 2m1f, for Sir Mark Prescott and rated 87; bought for 19,000gns last year and 50-1, never sighted on hurdles debut at Galway early this month; may need more time, but this is a much weaker maiden.

RaceName: Solar Generation Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Much improved in second bumper when allowed to dictate at Clonmel in May, trained then by Terence O'Brien; bought for 42,000GBP a week later and just okay yard debut at Galway early this month, having been made plenty of use of; entitled to come on for that and one to consider now switched to hurdles.

RaceName: Solar Generation Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Weak overall form in point-to-points and on bumper debut; never sighted on recent hurdles debut at Ballinrobe; tried in a tongue-tie now.

RaceName: Solar Generation Maiden Hurdle
OwnerName: A Cahill, M Dowd, P Glancy Partnership
Spotlight: Bought for 40,000GBP after winning a point-to-point last year; however, has struggled badly in a Sligo bumper and 2m5f Roscommon maiden hurdle; questions to answer now.

RaceName: Solar Generation Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Cost 55,000GBP as a 2yo; half-brother to four winners including French hurdle winners Norathir and Louvetot; dam Listed-placed French 1m3f/1m4f winner; Kilbeggan fifth was a step up on his Roscommon debut effort; more needed.

RaceName: Solar Generation Maiden Hurdle
Spotlight: Has shown potential in bumpers (including here) and ran a nice race on hurdles debut in 2m Tramore maiden in May (good); after a short break, was well below that form at Wexford last month (2m4f), reportedly blowing hard post-race; remains capable of better, so respected in a weak maiden.

RaceName: Solar Generation Maiden Hurdle
